title: Stockfish, But It Plays nth Best Move Where P(n) = (1/2)^n
summary: 'Geometric Fish': Stockfish picks its nth best move with probability (1/2)^n: 50% best, 25% 2nd best, 12.5% 3rd, 6.25% 4th, etc. Player (white) targets pieces that only have one defender so only the top move saves the bot, applies forcing pressure and eventually mates with a ladder mate (Rd6, Qc7+, Kf8, mate) to win game 1. Video also announces iwantcheckmate.com.
rules: Each bot move: rank all legal moves by engine eval; choose rank n with probability (1/2)^n (50% best, 25% 2nd, 12.5% 3rd, 6.25% 4th, ...).
(Inferred) leftover probability mass / fewer legal moves: renormalize.
Official site: considers Stockfish's top 6 ranked moves with weights 50%, 25%, 12%, 6%, 4%, 3%; leftover probability is added to the last available candidate.
win_condition: Checkmate the bot. Video: won game 1.
